name: WordPress
support: Open Source. Developed and maintained by the WordPress community.
technology: Server: PHP. Database: MySQL or MariaDB. Client: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Supports REST API.
capabilities: Thousands of themes and plugins. Custom page designs, blogging, e-commerce through WooCommerce, user management, and REST API support.
limitations: Requires regular updates and security maintenance. Poorly maintained plugins can create security risks. Some advanced features require paid plugins or development work.

name: Drupal
support: Open Source. Maintained by the Drupal community.
technology: Server: PHP. Database: MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, or SQLite. Client: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
capabilities: Custom content types, themes, modules, user permissions, multilingual support, and API capabilities. Suitable for large and complex websites.
limitations: Can be difficult for beginners to learn. Setup, configuration, and maintenance can require technical knowledge. Some projects need experienced developers.

name: Joomla
support: Open Source. Developed and supported by the Joomla community.
technology: Server: PHP. Database: MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL. Client: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
capabilities: Templates, extensions, user access controls, multilingual websites, content management, and customization options.
limitations: Some extensions and templates cost money. Updates and extension compatibility need attention. Beginners may need time to learn its administration system.

name: Wix
support: Commercial hosted website builder and CMS supported by Wix.
technology: Cloud-hosted platform. Wix manages the server and database infrastructure. Client: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Velo provides development tools and APIs.
capabilities: Drag-and-drop website editing, templates, content collections, dynamic pages, built-in hosting, and integrations. Supports custom development through Velo.
limitations: Less control over hosting and server configuration. Some features depend on paid plans. CMS collections have storage and usage limits. Moving a site to another platform can require rebuilding parts of it.

name: Shopify
support: Commercial hosted e-commerce platform supported by Shopify.
technology: Cloud-hosted platform with Shopify-managed database and infrastructure. Themes use Liquid, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Provides Storefront and other APIs.
capabilities: Online stores, product management, payment and checkout features, inventory management, themes, apps, and e-commerce APIs.
limitations: Monthly subscription costs and possible additional app fees. Advanced customization may require coding. Some checkout and platform features have restrictions. Less control over server infrastructure.
